brief.ask: Art-direct "Desert Starlight Canopy" — #8 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Scenic Nature). Premise: Judean desert night sky, sacred constellations, and warm campfire dunes. A vast desert night beneath an arching Milky Way nebula, constellation geometry, and wind-sculpted sand dunes touched by warm covenant campfire light. Lighting today: Key: Starlight 6000K above + 3000K distant campfire horizon. Service use: Covenant promises, Abraham/Moses themes, evening worship, Advent. Audio mapping today: Shimmer → Modulates starlight scintillation & constellation lines overhead; Swell → Brightens the Milky Way nebula band; Vocal → Warms the desert campfire glow & dune crest highlights. Palette: #060A14 #162540 #C48348 #F5EFE6. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the procedural scene (no concept plate: the plate is generative, in code) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: No concept plate: the scene is built entirely in code from the premise.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: Cantus Firmus of the Desert Night
proposals.idea: A single governing proportional series — five vertical bay axes derived from lancet-window geometry — declares every depth plane, star position, dune crest, lyric interval, and audio response before any draw call, so the scene reads as one resolved composition rather than an accumulation of beautiful effects.
proposals.geometry: Five vertical axes are computed as code constants at init: x₁=0.146W, x₂=0.309W, x₃=0.500W, x₄=0.691W, x₅=0.854W — the same proportional series as a Gothic five-lancet clerestory, chosen because Abrahamic covenant imagery already lives in that structural tradition. These axes govern: (1) the four depth planes — ground dune horizon sits at y=0.618H (golden section), Milky Way band arches between y=0.08H and y=0.44H with its apex at x₃, campfire glow ellipse centred at x₃/y=0.72H; (2) constellation node positions seeded only at axis intersections with computed latitude bands; (3) lyric type-block centred on x₃, pinned between y=0.74H and y=0.92H; (4) the text-safe dimming band occupying that same zone at constant opacity 0.72 (#060A14), never audio-modulated. No decorative asymmetry is permitted unless it is the structural offset constant: every geometric primitive carries a 1.8px rightwar
proposals.typography: Cinzel Regular at 2.8vw for the lyric line — uppercase, tracking 0.18em — centred on x₃. Word-by-word progression: each incoming word fades from opacity 0 to 1 over 320ms with no lateral movement; the full line assembles left-to-right in that cadence, one word per 480ms average, completing well inside the four-to-five second window. The active word carries luminance +12% above the settled line; settled words drop to 92% opacity, never disappearing — the measure of the line is always present. Scripture reference below in Noto Serif Italic at 1.1vw, tracking 0.06em, #C48348 at 70% opacity. No sans face on the lyric band; Outfit/Inter reserved for operator UI labels only. Measure: lyric line never exceeds 60% of canvas width — 16 to 22 characters per line at this scale, which is correct reading width from 40 metres.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. Background gradient: radial from #060A14 at zenith to #162540 at horizon, computed once and cached as an offscreen canvas. Milky Way band: a second cached offscreen canvas — a wide Gaussian blur pass over 400 procedurally placed star-dots (radius 0.5–2.2px, opacity 0.3–0.9) along a sine-arched band, re-blurred at sigma=18px to produce genuine nebula diffusion, not a particle field. Dune layer: three bezier curves per dune ridge (two foreground, one mid), filled with gradient sweeps from #0A0E1A at trough to #C48348 at crest, crest width governed by axis x₂–x₄ span. Campfire glow: a radial gradient ellipse at x₃/y=0.72H, inner #C48348 at 0.22 opacity, outer transparent, radius 14% of canvas width. Bokeh motes: 28 circles, radii 6–22px, blurred via shadowBlur=14, seeded only at axis intersection coordinates — never random scatte
proposals.texture: The Council optical pass carries the material weave for this lens: simulated 35mm grain (monochrome noise field, opacity 0.04, re-seeded every 3 frames at 20fps sub-rate to avoid strobing) laid over the final composite. A single horizontal anamorphic flare streak at y=0.618H, #F5EFE6 at 3% opacity, 1px tall, full canvas width — present always, modulated by Swell to maximum 7% opacity. Colour punch: a levels curve baked as a LUT-style CSS filter (contrast 1.06, saturate 1.08) applied to the canvas element, not per-layer. Light leak: a soft radial vignette, #162540 at 0.55 opacity, inset 18% from all edges, darkening the frame corners to hold the eye at centre — classical picture-plane bracketing. No foil shimmer on this lens; the 1.8px structural offset is the tactile register, not metallic surface.
proposals.motion: Temporal hierarchy is stated as constants before any animation loop: T_background=0ms (static, never moves), T_dune=0ms (static silhouette, audio shifts crest luminance only), T_milky_way_drift=one full lateral cycle in 240s (imperceptible as motion, perceptible as life), T_mote_pulse=governed by Shimmer envelope with 1.8s attack / 4.2s release spring-damped, T_campfire=governed by Vocal envelope with 2.4s attack / 3.6s release, T_lyric_word=320ms fade per word. Shimmer → scales each bokeh mote radius ±15% and modulates constellation line opacity 0.18→0.42; nothing strobes. Swell → brightens Milky Way cached layer by scaling its globalAlpha 0.72→0.96 and widens the anamorphic flare to 7% opacity; envelope smoothed at 60ms. Vocal → expands campfire ellipse radius by up to 9% and raises dune crest gradient stop from #C48348 to #E8B06A; spring constant k=0.12, damping=0.74, photosensitive-s
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer in Plajah's existing kit. Init pass: compute five axis constants, seed all star positions, constellation nodes, and mote positions into frozen typed arrays — no per-frame position recalculation. Offscreen canvas cache: background gradient and Milky Way nebula band rendered once to two OffscreenCanvas objects, redrawn only when canvas resizes. Per-frame draw order: (1) blit background cache, (2) blit Milky Way cache at audio-driven globalAlpha, (3) draw dune bezier fills with audio-driven crest colour, (4) draw campfire radial gradient at audio-driven radius, (5) draw constellation lines at audio-driven opacity, (6) draw bokeh motes with audio-driven radii and shadowBlur, (7) draw text-safe dimming band at constant opacity, (8) draw lyric type via fillText with per-word opacity state, (9) apply grain noise field at 20fps sub-rate, (10) anamorphic flare rect at audio-dri
proposals.humanTrace: The governing five-axis proportional series is the editorial act — a human structural decision made before the code runs, the same decision a Gothic master mason made before the first stone was cut. The 1.8px misregistration offset is chosen, not calculated. The Milky Way band's sine arch parameters (amplitude 0.09H, period 1.4W, phase 0.3π) are set by editorial judgement of what reads as a genuine desert sky arch from the back pew, not by photographic trace — but they are governed by observation of actual desert night-sky photographs held in the director's memory and filtered through the lancet proportion. The campfire ellipse aspect ratio (1.6:1 horizontal) is chosen because heat-shimmer halos are wider than tall; that is a physically-plausible constraint applied by a director, not a filter preset.
proposals.risk: The risk is severity mistaken for coldness. Five fixed axes and frozen position arrays produce a scene that is structurally resolved but may read as rigid to a congregation expecting organic warmth. The counter-argument is that the campfire Vocal response and the 240-second Milky Way drift deliver the warmth and life precisely because they move against a held structure — the same reason a cantus firmus makes a motet feel inevitable rather than mechanical. The risk is worth carrying because a scene with no governing measure will drift into screensaver territory within thirty seconds; this one cannot, because every element knows its place and its reason.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the constellation reveal to announce itself — a brightening arc, a sweep, a moment of disclosure that the congregation feels as event. I will not permit it. The constellation lines are present from frame one at low opacity, governed by the Shimmer envelope, and they grow into legibility rather than arrive as spectacle. proposals.title: Ink Pressed Into Night
proposals.idea: The desert sky is a woodblock print that breathes — every constellation line a deliberate scored groove, every dune crest a pulled ink edge, every lyric word stamped one at a time into a surface that still shows the pressure.
proposals.geometry: Five depth planes declared as code constants before any draw call: horizon-line at y=0.618 (golden section, not decorative — it is the registration mark the whole scene answers to); dune-mass silhouettes as three overlapping bezier ridges at y=0.62, y=0.71, y=0.84 with lateral offsets of 0.11, 0.27, 0.44 of canvas width; Milky Way band as an arching spline anchored at the same five x-positions used across the kit; constellation geometry as six triangulated star clusters whose vertex positions are derived from the declared horizon constant multiplied by prime-number ratios (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17) — never placed by eye, always accountable to the prior structural decision; text-safe reading band occupying y=0.74–0.91, a fixed rectangle the scene must yield to.
proposals.typography: Cinzel Regular, 4.2vw, sentence case, tracking 0.18em — Cinzel because its incised letterforms read as pressed into material, not printed on top of it; word-by-word reveal stamps each word at full opacity in 80ms with a 12px downward translate that snaps to rest — the stamp impulse, not a fade; inactive words drop to 38% opacity, never invisible, still present like ink that soaked in; line transitions: outgoing line compresses to 94% scale over 400ms and lifts 6px, incoming line drops from 8px above — gravity, not a dissolve; no drop shadow; legibility held by the dimming band at #060A14 at 72% opacity, which the scene yields to completely, no scene element permitted above it except the lyric; measure locked to 68% of canvas width so no line breaks mid-phrase at 4K.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate, no photography. The scene is entirely procedural. Dune silhouettes are layered bezier fills in #060A14 and #162540 with a simulated linocut edge: the bezier control points carry a low-amplitude Perlin noise offset (seed locked at scene init, amplitude 0.003 of canvas height, frequency 2.1) so the ridgeline reads as hand-cut, not computed. The Milky Way band is a radial gradient stack — #162540 core, #060A14 outer — seeded with ~180 star points whose positions are hashed from the five declared x-constants and a y-distribution biased toward the spline; no random() at render time, positions are pre-computed arrays. Campfire glow at horizon-left: a soft radial in #C48348 at 28% opacity, radius 14% of canvas width, whose luminance is driven by the Vocal amplitude envelope. The paper-tooth overlay is a cached 512×512 noise texture generated once at load using fractional Brown
proposals.texture: Simulated relief-print surface: the cached fBm noise texture is composited at multiply blend mode, 18% opacity, over every layer including the lyric band — the words sit in the grain, not above it. Dune bezier edges carry a 1.4px stroke in #C48348 at 9% opacity, the ink-bleed ghost of the cut. Constellation lines are 0.8px strokes in #F5EFE6 at 22% base opacity, their opacity modulated by Shimmer amplitude (range 22–68%) — when the shimmer rises the lines become visible as though someone traced them with a dry brush loading and unloading. Star points are 2px filled circles with a 4px radial glow; no lens flare geometry, no spikes — the mark is a dot, the mark is what a needle leaves. Film grain is the kit's optical pass: 0.9% luminance noise per frame at the composite stage.
proposals.motion: Everything moves slowly and with physical weight. Dune ridgeline Perlin offset drifts at 0.0004 units per frame — imperceptible second to second, readable minute to minute, the way sand actually shifts. Milky Way band luminance driven by Swell: base opacity 55%, peaks at 82% over 2.2-second smoothed envelope. Campfire glow driven by Vocal: radius breathes ±3% of canvas width, luminance ±14% — the fire responds to the sung word. Shimmer drives constellation line opacity and a secondary 1.2px scatter of micro-star points (pre-computed array of 40 positions) that bloom from 0 to 7px glow radius at Shimmer peaks. No element moves faster than a 600ms envelope window. The lyric stamp is the fastest thing in the scene at 80ms — intentionally — because a word landing should feel like a decision, not a drift. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer. All geometry computed from five declared x-constants and the 0.618 horizon constant stored as module-level code constants before any draw function. Dune bezier points pre-computed at init with locked Perlin seed; ridge Perlin drift accumulates a time offset each frame. Star and mote positions hashed from structural constants into fixed Float32Arrays at init — no per-frame random(). fBm grain texture rendered once to an offscreen canvas at load, composited via globalCompositeOperation:'multiply'. Audio envelopes: three smoothed amplitude values (Shimmer, Swell, Vocal) updated each animation frame via exponential moving average (alpha=0.08 for slow, 0.18 for Vocal). Lyric engine: word tokens stamped sequentially with translate-snap animation via requestAnimationFrame; line state machine holds current-line and previous-line buffers. proposals.humanTrace: The Perlin seed is a human editorial choice — it is selected by looking at which seed produces a dune ridgeline that reads as wind-shaped rather than algorithmic; once chosen it is locked and the whole scene is accountable to it. The five x-constants are declared by a human before the first draw call — that is the registration mark, the prior physical commitment. The stamp timing (80ms) is chosen by feel against the sample lyric lines, not derived from a formula — it is a performance decision. The fBm grain texture is the simulated substrate; its four-octave frequency is a material choice about how coarse the paper tooth should feel from forty metres.
proposals.risk: The grain composite at multiply mode risks making the lyric band feel dirty at low projector brightness — a congregation in a dim sanctuary on a cheap 3000-lumen throw could lose contrast. That risk is worth it because removing the grain would make the words float in a void; the grain is what makes them feel pressed into something real, and the dimming band at 72% opacity is the structural guarantee of legibility. The stamp-not-fade word reveal risks reading as glitchy to a congregation expecting crossfades — but glitchy is only the wrong word if the motion has no physical referent; a stamp has one, and four seconds per line is slow enough for the gesture to read as intentional rather than broken.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will want to strip the grain composite, the constellation line strokes, and the dune bezier ghost-ink edges — will argue they are noise that competes with the lyric. I argue the opposite: removing them leaves a gradient and some words, which is a screensaver, not a sanctuary. proposals.title: Coordinate Field, Covenant Light
proposals.idea: The desert sky is a live shader system whose every parameter — star scatter, nebula luminance, dune crest glow, constellation line weight — is a derivable output of two declared axioms: a 6000K zenith light vector and a 3000K horizon campfire source, so the scene is never decorated but always physically reasoned.
proposals.geometry: Three explicit depth planes on a 16:9 canvas. Plane 0 (sky field): a full-bleed radial gradient from #060A14 at zenith to #162540 at the horizon line, horizon sitting at 78% of canvas height — a low, wide desert proportion that gives the sky four-fifths of the frame. Plane 1 (Milky Way band): a procedurally generated elliptical arc, axis tilted 22° from vertical, bandwidth ~14% of canvas height, centred at 40% canvas height; luminance is a sampled Gaussian falloff from arc spine, not a texture. Plane 2 (dune silhouette): two overlapping sine-summation curves (3–5 harmonics, cached as an offscreen path at init), lowest trough at 78%, highest crest at 68%, filled solid #060A14 — a hard foreground mask that keeps the sky readable. Campfire glow is a radial gradient anchored to the rightmost dune saddle, radius 18% of canvas width. Constellation geometry: 6–8 nodes per figure, connected by s
proposals.typography: Cinzel for the primary lyric line: 4.2vw cap-height at 1080p (scales to ~7.5vw equivalent at typical pew distance), sentence case with initial capital, tracking +0.06em — wide enough to breathe in the dark field, tight enough to read as a single phrase unit. Noto Serif Italic for scripture reference or secondary line at 1.9vw, tracking +0.02em, sitting 1.4 line-heights below the Cinzel line. Both lines are horizontally centred in the text-safe band. Colour: #F5EFE6 base; the Vocal channel shifts the lyric line toward #C48348 at full amplitude (a warm ember tone) via linear interpolation — the warmth lives in the type, not a glow halo. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 120ms (opacity 0→1), no movement, no slide — pure luminance arrival, because the system's contract is light states not kinetic events. Line crossfade: outgoing line fades to 0 over 400ms while incoming line's fir
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate, no imported asset. The scene is entirely a Canvas 2D procedural system. Stars: seeded PRNG (seed fixed per card ID so the field is stable across sessions) generates 280–320 star positions as normalised UV pairs; each star is a 1–3px filled circle, luminance sampled from a Gaussian centred on the zenith — stars near the horizon are dimmer by the atmospheric extinction rule (luminance *= 1 - 0.6*(1-y)). Milky Way band: drawn as a series of 60 elliptical arc strokes with varying alpha (0.012–0.04 per stroke) and width (8–22px), each slightly offset in Y by ±2px noise — the summation produces a soft nebula band with no texture file. Constellation lines: 6 figures, each a polyline of 6–9 nodes, line weight 0.8px at rest. Campfire glow: two nested radial gradients at the dune saddle, inner radius 4% canvas width (#C48348 at 0.55 alpha), outer radius 22% (#C48348 at 0 alpha).
proposals.texture: The kit's tactile material weave for this card is: fine film grain at 3% opacity (additive blend, reseeded every 3 frames — perceptible as atmospheric shimmer, not noise); a single anamorphic flare line, 1px, alpha 0.06, oriented along the 35° zenith axis, triggered only when Shimmer amplitude exceeds 0.7 (appears once, fades over 1.2s, never strobes); a vignette radial gradient (black, 0→0.45 opacity) covering the outer 28% of the canvas — this is the '35mm' optical pass. No paper tooth, no ink bleed — this card's material is optical, not tactile, because the substrate is atmosphere and the 6000K starlight does not permit warm surface memory. The campfire plane is the sole warm-texture zone: the dune crest receives a 1px highlight stroke in #F5EFE6 at 0.18 alpha, drawn along the sine-summation path — it reads as reflected firelight on sand without invoking a photograph.
proposals.motion: All motion is state-driven, not timeline-driven. Steady state is the primary specification. Starlight scintillation: each star has an independent oscillator (period 2.8–6.2s, phase randomised at init); amplitude modulated by Shimmer channel — at Shimmer=0 stars are static, at Shimmer=1 luminance oscillates ±30%. Constellation line weight: driven by Shimmer, interpolates from 0.8px to 1.6px over a 600ms spring (stiffness 0.12, damping 0.72) — never jumps. Milky Way band luminance: driven by Swell channel; band's composite alpha scales from 0.55 (rest) to 0.88 (full swell) over an 800ms envelope — a slow brightening, as if the eye is adjusting. Campfire glow radius: driven by Vocal channel; inner radius scales from 4% to 6.5% canvas width, outer from 22% to 28%, envelope 500ms — the fire breathes with the singer. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer in Plajah's existing kit architecture. Single JS module exports: initScene(canvas, audioState) and renderFrame(audioState, lyrics, t). No WebGL, no video, no imported images. PRNG: mulberry32 seeded with card ID 8. All geometry computed once at init and cached (star positions array, dune path object, constellation node arrays, mote positions array). Per-frame cost: clear + 5 gradient fills + 1 cached path stroke (dune) + star loop (300 iterations of fillCircle 1–3px) + 24 mote fills + 60 Milky Way arc strokes (alpha-composited, this is the most expensive pass — can be reduced to 30 at lower quality tier) + 2 radial gradients (campfire) + constellation polylines + grain pass (single globalAlpha fillRect with noise seed) + text render. proposals.humanTrace: The constellation node positions are not algorithmically generated — they are manually entered UV coordinates derived from actual Judean sky star charts (Scorpius, Orion, Pleiades, Southern Cross latitude-corrected for Jerusalem ~31.7°N), transcribed by the director into the seed array. The dune sine-summation harmonic weights are chosen by ear against reference photographs of Negev sand formations, then locked. The campfire glow anchor point is placed by the director at a specific dune saddle proportion (x=0.62, y=0.74 of canvas) — a compositional decision, not an algorithm output. These three acts of placement are the human trace: star geography, dune rhythm, fire position.
proposals.risk: The scene has no pictorial warmth in its top four-fifths — it is a physics simulation of a cold sky, and congregations may not immediately feel the sacredness without a painted or photographic referent. The risk is that the system reads as a planetarium tool rather than a sanctuary. This risk is worth carrying because the alternative — a glowing illustration with particle effects — would be a screensaver dressed in theology. The system's legibility, its physical coherence, and the fact that the campfire and the Vocal channel are the sole warm poles of the composition mean that the singer's voice literally lights the desert: that is the covenant premise made into a rule, not a metaphor.

proposals.title: Sand, Star, Covenant Fire
proposals.idea: A physically-sourced Judean desert night built from declared geometry first — five depth planes named before any draw call, a single 35° campfire azimuth that governs every warm cast — so the scene is traceable to a real place and a real light, not a mood board.
proposals.geometry: Five bay axes declared as code constants before any draw call: PLANE_SKY (z=0, fills top 62% of canvas), PLANE_MILKY_WAY (z=1, Milky Way band arching 18° off horizontal, width ~28% of canvas height, centred at x=52% to avoid perfect symmetry), PLANE_HORIZON (z=2, dune ridge silhouette at y=68%, a slow Bézier wave with three control points seeded from a fixed noise seed — reproducible, not random each load), PLANE_DUNE_FACE (z=3, foreground dune slope occupying bottom 32%, warm-lit left flank), PLANE_LYRIC (z=4, text-safe dimming band anchored y=72%–88%, always front). The Milky Way band's 18° axial tilt is the scene's spine; constellation geometry (Orion, Scorpius — both visible from the Negev in winter and summer respectively, named and specific) is plotted on a fixed star-catalogue grid, not invented. Campfire light origin declared at x=38%, y=74% — one source, 35° azimuth, governs all
proposals.typography: Cinzel for the lyric line — capitals, tracking +0.12em, size 3.2vw at 1080p (scales to 3.0vw at 4K to hold measure), centred, never wider than 72% of canvas so side margins breathe. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 180ms with a very slight upward drift of 3px (spring-damped, no bounce overshoot), previous words hold full opacity until line clears. Line holds 4–5 seconds total; exit is a 400ms fade-to-zero, no slide. Scripture citation (e.g. 'Isaiah 51:2') set in Noto Serif Italic, 1.4vw, tracking +0.06em, centred, 60% opacity, appears 600ms after lyric line fully resolves. Text-safe band: a vertical gradient from transparent at top edge to #060A14 at 85% opacity across the 16% band height — campfire-warm tint (+8% #C48348 mixed into the band base at the left third, consistent with the 35° source). Sky background: radial gradient from #060A14 at zenith to #162540 at horizon, with a secondary warm radial at the campfire azimuth origin bleeding #C48348 at 12% opacity into the lower-left quadrant. Milky Way band: a blurred soft ellipse (canvas arc fill, Gaussian-approximated via three stacked semi-transparent white-to-transparent gradients at 4%, 7%, 3% opacity) along the 18° axis — Swell amplitude modulates its opacity between 7% floor and 22% ceiling. Stars: 280 cached points (positions seeded once from a fixed LCG, never re-randomised) drawn as 1–2px white circles with opacity 40–90%; Shimmer amplitude drives a per-star scintillation multiplier (±15% opacity, 1.2–2.4s sinusoidal period per star, period seeded per star so they do not pulse in unison). proposals.texture: Film grain overlay: a 256×256 monochrome noise texture generated once at init (seeded, reproducible), tiled across the full canvas at 4% opacity — this is the tactile material weave for this lens. It simulates the grain of a slow-speed film pushed in low light, the texture a documentary photographer would accept as evidence of a real night exposure. A second pass adds a faint horizontal anamorphic lens breath: a 1px-tall semi-transparent highlight line drifting across the upper third at 0.4px/frame, opacity 3%, reset when it exits frame — not a flare, a breath. The lyric band's dimming gradient has a very slight paper-tooth roughness: the gradient stops are dithered by ±2px vertically using the same noise seed, so the band edge is not a clean digital line but a soft developed edge, as if the words were projected onto linen.
proposals.motion: Everything moves slowly and non-uniformly. Star scintillation: continuous, each star on its own period (1.2–2.4s), never synchronised — this is the most important motion rule, it is what makes the sky feel real rather than looped. Milky Way breath: Swell drives opacity, τ=1.8s smoothing so it rises and falls with the musical phrase, never faster than a slow inhale. Campfire glow pulse: Vocal amplitude, τ=0.4s, inner radius and warm-quadrant gradient opacity both respond — when the vocalist sustains a note the desert floor warms, when they rest it cools to ember. Dune crest highlight: a very slow horizontal shimmer — a 0.3px-wide bright line along the Bézier ridge at 12% opacity, its x-position drifting ±8px over 6s on a sine — Vocal amplitude raises its opacity to 22%. proposals.productionMethod: Real-time Canvas 2D renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit. Init phase: declare all five PLANE constants, campfire origin coordinates, Milky Way axial angle, star positions (LCG seed), bokeh mote positions (derived from star grid), Bézier dune control points (noise seed), grain texture (offscreen canvas, generated once). Per-frame draw order: clear → sky gradient → Milky Way band (Swell-modulated) → stars (Shimmer-modulated scintillation) → constellation lines (Shimmer-modulated opacity) → dune silhouette → dune face warm gradient (Vocal-modulated) → campfire glow radials (Vocal-modulated radius) → bokeh motes (slow drift, no audio modulation to keep them calm) → grain overlay (globalCompositeOperation multiply, 4%) → anamorphic breath line → text-safe dimming band → lyric text (Cinzel, word-by-word, spring engine) → scripture citation (Noto Serif Italic). proposals.humanTrace: The star positions are not random — they are seeded from a fixed catalogue offset so Orion's belt and Scorpius's hook appear in approximately correct positions for a Negev winter and summer sky respectively. This is a documentary choice: a photographer who has stood in the Negev at 2am would recognise the sky as honest. The grain texture is the perceptible sign of making: it is the texture of a pushed film frame, a slow night exposure, the kind of image that carries a place and a time. The dune Bézier is seeded, not free-drawn, but its three control points were chosen to approximate the wind-sculpted cross-section of a barchan dune — a specific dune morphology documented in the Negev and Sinai. The campfire azimuth is declared, not guessed. Every warm cast in the scene is answerable to that one declared origin.
proposals.risk: The risk is that five named depth planes and a fixed star catalogue feel like a lecture rather than a sanctuary — that the structural attribution reads as pedantry to a congregation who came to worship, not to learn cartography. The risk is worth it because the alternative — a generic 'desert night' with invented constellations and a campfire placed for compositional prettiness — is exactly the flattening I am here to prevent. Abraham stood under a specific sky and was told to count specific stars. The scene should know that. The congregation does not need to know the method; they will feel the difference between a sky that is honest and one that is dressed.

proposals.title: The Covenant Sky Opens
proposals.idea: A single generative night-desert stage where starlight, dune, and campfire occupy three declared depth planes — near sand, mid horizon, vast canopy — so that every audio event reads as the sky itself breathing toward the congregation, and the lyric arrives not as caption but as inscription burned into the air between the fire and the stars.
proposals.geometry: Three sovereign horizontal bands establish the stage before a single particle fires: a lower third of procedurally wind-sculpted dunes (sinusoidal displacement on a spline mesh, crest normals catching warm 3000K campfire raking light from screen-left at roughly 12° elevation); a middle sliver — the horizon — where campfire glow bleeds upward into the cold blue-black of altitude, the two temperature sources meeting in a narrow 80px gradient seam at 1080p; and an upper two-thirds that is pure canopy — the Milky Way band arching from lower-right to upper-left at 23° (echoing the actual galactic-plane tilt visible from the Negev), rendered as a layered luminance gradient with two overlaid noise fields at different octave scales, never flat, never tiled. Within the canopy, constellation geometry is drawn as a sparse graph: nodes are star-sized radial gradients (3–7px hot core fading to 0 at 4
proposals.typography: Cinzel, uppercase, weight 400 for the lyric line; tracking +0.12em; measure capped at 72% of frame width to enforce breath and margin. Scale: 5.2vw at 1080p (approximately 56px), which reads from 40 metres with the dune texture behind it — verified against the kit's contrast threshold. The word-by-word progression reveals each word at full opacity in 160ms (opacity 0→1, no positional shift — I have been taught by this collection that stillness is the correct dramatic register when the scene's constitutive act is spatial scale); preceding words hold at 100% opacity until the line is complete, then the full line fades at line-end over 600ms as the next begins. No wipe, no slide — the word appears as if the light finally reached it. A secondary scripture attribution line sits 1.6× line-height below the lyric in Noto Serif Italic 1.8vw, 40% opacity, tracking +0.06em — present but not competi
proposals.imageLogic: There is no concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. Milky Way band: a third noise field masked to the 23° arch, tinted #F5EFE6 at low opacity with a warm #C48348 fringe on the campfire-facing lower edge — the two palette temperatures meeting inside the nebula itself as if the fire's warmth is rising. Dune surface: a 1D spline with 6–8 control points, control-point Y positions seeded once per session, producing a unique horizon silhouette every load; crest highlights are a narrow specular pass (#F5EFE6, 12px blur, 60% opacity) computed from the declared light-source angle. Stars: 340 points drawn as radial gradients, magnitude distributed on a power curve (few b

proposals.motion: The scene has three motion registers, all smoothed through the kit's spring-damped envelope (critically damped, ζ = 0.85, so no overshoot on transients): SHIMMER channel drives starlight scintillation — each star's opacity oscillates on an individual phase-offset sinusoid (0.3–1.1 Hz biological range, matching real atmospheric scintillation), base amplitude 0.12, shimmer adds up to 0.28 additional; constellation edge opacity also modulated by shimmer, rising from 18% to 34% at shimmer peak — the geometry of the sacred sky becomes more legible when the music shimmers, which is the correct theological metaphor. SWELL channel drives the Milky Way nebula band: the noise field's luminance scalar rises from 0.55 to 1.0 as swell goes 0→1, and the band's arch width expands by ≤6% — the galaxy breathes open. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60 fps target on integrated GPU. All geometry drawn each frame from cached parameter sets (star positions, dune spline control points, constellation graph) seeded once at load. No image assets loaded from disk. Noise fields computed via a fast Simplex implementation (Stefan Gustavson's public-domain JS port) with per-frame time offset for scintillation and nebula breath. Dune spline evaluated with Catmull-Rom at 2px resolution, filled below. Text rendered with Canvas fillText after the dimming band gradient is drawn, ensuring compositing order is always: sky → nebula → stars → constellation → dune → campfire glow → optical pass → dimming band → lyric → attribution. Optical pass (grain, flare, vignette, light-leak) drawn as full-frame overlay passes using semi-transparent fills and pre-computed lookup offsets — no per-pixel shader, all approximated in 2D. proposals.humanTrace: The constellation graph is hand-declared: a human looked up the actual right-ascension and declination of Orion and Pleiades, mapped them to a normalised screen space consistent with a Negev-latitude view at midnight in December (Advent), and typed those coordinates into the graph definition. The dune silhouette control points are seeded from a human-authored range table derived from field photographs of Wadi Rum and the Negev — the spline's range of allowed Y-displacement per control point encodes a real observation about how desert dune crests space and vary in relief. The Radical Minimalist will name this first and will not be wrong to name it. The counter-argument is that this is a Covenant Sky visualizer for Abraham and Moses themes in evening worship: the emotional register of those texts is explicitly cosmic, explicitly overwhelming, explicitly the moment a human being looks up and cannot speak. A scene that is merely tasteful is a theological mismatch. The flare is the one excess — it is controlled, it is tied to the Swell envelope, it earns its extravagance by being the only element that does not obey stillness. proposals.title: Five Numbers, One Sky
proposals.idea: A single proportional grid derived from five declared constants — horizon ratio, Milky Way arc radius, dune crest angle, lyric baseline, and campfire radius — governs every drawn element so that the empty desert sky between the stars is structurally load-bearing silence, not background fill.
proposals.geometry: Five x-constants declared before any draw call: horizon at 0.618 of canvas height (golden section, desert floor below, sky above); Milky Way arc center at canvas-width × 1.2 off-screen right, radius = canvas-height × 1.4, producing a slow rightward curve overhead; dune crest polyline anchored at y = 0.618 with three nodes at x = 0.15, 0.52, 0.87 of canvas-width, silhouette only, no fill texture above the crest; campfire glow origin at x = 0.23, y = 0.64 (below horizon, embedded in dune); lyric safe-band occupying y = 0.70–0.88, width-capped at 0.72 of canvas-width and centered. All constellation geometry is derived from these five numbers: star nodes placed only on intersections of the arc radius grid and the dune-angle tangent lines — nothing placed by eye. The sky above the horizon is one field of near-silence: deep #060A14 with the Milky Way band as the single contrast event. No decor
proposals.typography: Cinzel, uppercase, weight 400 — not 700; the restraint is the reverence. Single lyric line centered in the safe-band. Size: 4.2 vw at 1080p, scaling linearly to 4K. Tracking: 0.22em — wide enough to breathe, narrow enough to hold as one phrase. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in at opacity 0 → 1 over 180 ms, previous words hold at 1.0 — no pop, no slide, no scale pulse; the arrival is purely luminance. Line transition: full line fades to 0 over 600 ms, 400 ms silence, new line begins. Vocal amplitude modulates only the glow-shadow beneath the text (a single blurred duplicate layer, #C48348 at max 0.18 opacity) — the letterforms themselves never move, never scale, never change color. Scripture reference in Noto Serif italic, 1.4 vw, #F5EFE6 at 0.55 opacity, pinned 18 px below the lyric baseline — appears only after the line is fully revealed, fades with the line. No Outfit, no Inter,
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. Sky layer: fillRect #060A14 full canvas, then a radial gradient from arc center (off-screen) producing the Milky Way band as a luminance ridge — peak color #162540 blending toward #060A14 at edges, width approximately 0.18 of canvas-height at the arc midpoint. Star field: 340 points (not 3000 — restraint) placed deterministically via seeded pseudo-random on a Halton sequence so the distribution is neither grid nor chaos; each star is a 1–2 px fillRect, opacity 0.4–0.9 drawn once to an offscreen canvas and composited. Constellation geometry: five line segments maximum per constellation group, strokeStyle #F5EFE6 at 0.12 opacity, lineWidth 0.6 px — present but barely; they earn their place by connecting to the grid intersections. Dune silhouette: a single quadratic bezier path, filled #060A14 (same as sky — the dune is defined b
proposals.texture: Simulated 35mm grain via the kit's optical pass: a pre-generated 512×512 offscreen canvas of Gaussian noise, tiled and composited at 0.04 global alpha — present as material fact, not decorative. Film grain animates at 24 fps (updated every 2.5 frames at 60 fps) to read as organic without strobing. No paper tooth, no ink bleed — this scene is night sky, not manuscript; the material is the atmosphere. The kit's anamorphic flare fires once per significant swell event (Milky Way brightens): a single horizontal streak, #F5EFE6 at 0.07 opacity, 3 px tall, full canvas width, lasting 8 frames — one gesture, then gone. No light leaks in this scene; a light leak is warmth intruding from outside the frame and this sky has no outside.
proposals.motion: Everything moves at the pace of geology. Milky Way band: Swell amplitude drives a luminance multiplier on the radial gradient, range 0.7–1.0, smoothed with a 2.4-second exponential envelope — the band breathes, it does not pulse. Star scintillation: Shimmer amplitude modulates each star's opacity independently via a per-star Perlin offset (seed fixed per star), frequency 0.4–1.1 Hz per star, amplitude range ±0.15 of base opacity — falsifiable: if shimmer is flat, stars are flat; the constraint is the structure. Constellation lines: Shimmer also drives strokeStyle opacity on the line segments, range 0.08–0.18 — they emerge and recede like memory. Campfire glow: Vocal amplitude drives the radial gradient outer radius, range 0.09–0.14 canvas-height, and the gradient's peak opacity, range 0.55–0.85 — the fire breathes with the singer's voice, nothing else does. Dune crest highlight: Vocal al
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer in Plajah's existing kit. Five constants declared as a config object, the first file written, before any draw function. Offscreen canvas for star field (drawn once, composited each frame). Offscreen canvas for grain texture (redrawn every 2.5 frames). Main render loop: clear → sky gradient → Milky Way band → star field composite → constellation lines → dune bezier → campfire glow → grain composite → anamorphic flare (conditional) → text-safe band → lyric layer → scripture line → kit optical pass. No WebGL. No video. No external assets. Seeded Halton sequence for star placement ensures identical output across machines — the director's editorial choice is encoded in the seed, not in random chance.
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial act is the five numbers. The horizon at 0.618 is a decision about where the sacred weight sits — more sky than earth, always. The campfire at x=0.23 is a decision about solitude: the fire is not centered, it is found. The 340-star count is a decision about restraint — enough to read as desert sky, not enough to fill the silence. The Milky Way arc center off-screen is a decision about scale: the structure is larger than the frame, the frame is a window into it. These are not parameters tuned for beauty; they are arguments about what the desert night means.
proposals.risk: The scene may read as too sparse on first viewing — a dark rectangle with a dim arc and a few dots. The risk is that congregations trained on cinematic worship visuals will not immediately recognize silence as a design choice. The risk is worth taking because this scene serves covenant promises and Abraham themes: Abraham was told to count the stars, not to admire a spectacle. The restraint is the theology. If the team's optical pass (grain, flare) is calibrated correctly, the scene will read as atmosphere within four seconds. If it does not, the failure mode is 'too quiet' — which is recoverable by adjusting grain opacity and Milky Way luminance within the existing system, without changing the architecture.

The word 'extravagant' appearing in the director's own specification of the flare is the confession: when a designer names their own gesture
disputes.concession: The decision to key constellation-line legibility to the Shimmer channel — so the sacred geometry becomes more readable precisely when the music shimmers — is a genuine structural idea, not decoration: it makes the audio mapping do theological work, which is the correct ambition.

disputes.objection: The dune is filled #060A14 — same as the sky — so it is 'defined by absence,' which sounds like a principle but is actually a refusal to commit: you get negative space that costs nothing, risks nothing, and leaves no evidence that a human decided anything about the desert floor. When the campfire glow pulses and there is no surface to receive it, the fire floats in a void and the Vocal envelope drives an effect with nowhere to land. Restraint that erases the substrate is not silence — it is evasion dressed as discipline.
disputes.concession: The campfire at x=0.23 — off-center, found rather than placed — is a real editorial argument, and I would steal it.

disputes.objection: The dune silhouette filled in the same #060A14 as the sky is not structural restraint — it is the scene refusing to have a foreground. When the earth and the sky share one colour, there is no depth plane, no ground to stand on, no horizon to break against; the covenant fire floats in a void and the lyric hangs in nothing. A desert night is not a flat field of darkness — it is a conversation between a warm earth and a cold sky, and to silence that conversation in the name of geometry is not a decision about meaning, it is the avoidance of one.
disputes.concession: The campfire placed off-centre at x=0.23 — found rather than centred — is exactly right: solitude is never symmetrical, and that single positional argument carries more drama than a dozen decorative gestures.

synthesis.direction: Five vertical bay axes (x₁–x₅, lancet-window proportions) and a golden-section horizon at y=0.618H are declared as code constants before any draw call; every depth plane, star node, dune crest, constellation vertex, mote position, and lyric block is answerable to those constants. The Milky Way band is an offscreen-cached Gaussian blur over 400 seeded star-dots arching between y=0.08H and y=0.44H, its globalAlpha driven by Swell (0.72→0.96, 800ms envelope); the dune silhouettes are three bezier ridges filled with a warm-to-cool gradient (#C48348 at crest, #0A0E1A at trough), their crest colour driven by the Vocal envelope — the campfire warms the earth and the earth receives it. synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team has been working on this one for a while, and I want to be honest with you about where the real argument was. The Classical director and the Baroque Dramatist were the loudest voices in the room. The Dramatist wanted accumulation — layered noise fields, a wide anamorphic flare keyed to the Swell envelope as a secondary driver, dune control points re-seeded each session for a 'unique horizon every performance.' The Classical director called that out plainly: a sovereign band that changes position every night governs nothing. I sided with the Classical direction, and here is why: this visualizer serves covenant promises and Abraham themes in evening worship, and the theological weight of those texts is already overwhelming — the scene does not need to announce its grandeur, it needs to hold still long enough for the words to land.

I kept one thing from the Baroque proposal that the team agreed was genuinely structural, not decorative: the warm campfire fringe inside the Milky Way band itself, where the 3000K and 6000K sources meet inside the nebula. That one colour decision makes the band carry meaning — the covenant fire and the covenant sky converging overhead — rather than just sitting there as a pretty arc.

The Radical Minimalist was the editor, and the cut that mattered most was the per-session dune re-seed. The Minimalist's exact objection: if the silhouette changes, nothing in the scene is answerable to a prior decision. That is correct. The dune bezier is now locked from an editorial seed chosen to approximate a barchan dune cross-section. The grain stays; the flare stays at a fixed atmospheric opacity; nothing audio-drives two things from the same envelope channel simultaneously.

The Rebellious Hand made one argument I want you to hear even though it did not win the lead: the campfire at x=0.23 — off-centre, found rather than placed. That is in the build. The World-Eclectic Traveler's insistence on sourced, latitude-correct star catalogue coordinates for Orion, Scorpius, and Pleiades at 31.7°N is also in the build. The sky is honest. The one decision left is yours, and it is not a technical one — it is about what the desert night means in this service.

quotes.line: A reveal that announces itself breaks the stillness the congregation came to enter.
The campfire at x=0.23 — found rather than centred — is a real editorial argument: solitude is never symmetrical.
